Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment uses an AP-MS approach to purify translation products of modified mRNAs using a Flag-tag. While the study focuses on RNA modifications (inosine, etc.), the proteomics part is a standard bottom-up DDA run of the resulting proteins to verify amino acid incorporation. No PTM enrichment (like phospho or ubiquitin) was performed on the proteins themselves.

Ontology_TreatmentAndDesign_prompt.notes: The study uses mass spectrometry to identify the amino acids incorporated when non-standard nucleotides are used as inputs in the mRNA template, comparing these to standard translation. This is a modified biomolecule input comparison.

base_candidates_ranked.reason: The experiment uses DDA (Q Exactive HF) and focuses on identifying specific amino acid substitutions (miscoding) in translated peptides. While not a large-scale LFQ study, the analysis of 'translation levels' and 'abundance' of peptide variants suggests a label-free approach.

workflow: Peptides were analyzed using a Dionex, UltiMate 3000 nano-HPLC system coupled via nanospray ionization source to a Thermo Scientific Q Exactive HF mass spectrometer
Database search was performed using ProteomeDiscoverer (Version 2.1, Thermo Scientific) with search engine Sequest HT
Enzyme for protein cleavage was trypsin; two missed cleavages were allowed
differential: the interpretation of these RNA nucleobase derivatives by the ribosomal decoding site was also determined
the translated peptides from the bacterial and eukaryotic systems were purified and analyzed by mass spectrometry (MS)
search_parameters: Fixed modification was carbamidomethylcysteine; variable modifications were N-terminal protein acetylation and methionine oxidation
Precursor mass tolerance was set to 10 ppm; fragment mass tolerance was 20 mmu

Ontology_ProcessingAndDifferential_promp.notes: The experiment is specifically designed to detect amino acid substitutions resulting from non-standard codon translation (miscoding). The search database was customized by adding 21 different ErmCL protein sequences to the human reference proteome to capture these specific variants.
